nodes.text: OpenAI Agents SDK Session is a runtime_checkable async Protocol with session_id, session_settings and four methods: get_items(limit), add_items(items), pop_item(), clear_session(). Granularity is item-level (append, pop-last, clear), not whole history. SessionABC exists but third parties are told to implement the Protocol.

OpenAI Agents SDK ships many backends: SQLite (sync and async), Redis, SQLAlchemy, MongoDB, Dapr, OpenAIConversationsSession (server-side), compaction wrapper, AdvancedSQLite, EncryptedSession; community Django. H1 confirmed and extended.

OpenAI Agents SDK stores each history item as its own JSON text row (json.dumps of the Responses-API input item), so the format is the OpenAI Responses item shape; no version field or migration mechanism was seen in the SQLite/SQLAlchemy backends, and unparsable SQLite rows are skipped silently.
nodes.limitations: Absence of a versioning mechanism inferred from reading two backend files, not an explicit doc statement.

nodes.text: OpenAI Agents SDK leaves session id ownership and authorization to the host: the id selects history but does not authenticate or authorize. Concurrency is backend-level: SQLAlchemy serializes mutations per session with a lock and atomic tail pop (DELETE RETURNING / FOR UPDATE); SQLite uses process-wide per-path locks; there is no turn-level lock or conflict detection.
nodes.limitations: Turn-level concurrency (two runs on one session) not documented in pages read; inferred from absence.

nodes.text: Pydantic AI has moved beyond H2: docs now recommend storing a Conversation (messages, usage, conversation_id, deferred tool requests) rather than messages alone, and offer an abstract ConversationStore (ABC) with five async primitives: read_record, read_records(scope, limit), write_record(record, new_entries, expected_revision), delete_record(id, expected_revision), read_entry. Only InMemoryConversationStore ships (tests/examples); production backends are host-written; the DB schema is left to the host.
nodes.applicability: Based on Pydantic AI docs as of 2026-11; API appears recent and may still change.

nodes.text: Pydantic AI stores conversations as an append-only log where each message is stored once (forks share entries), with optimistic concurrency: save checks a revision and raises ConversationConflict instead of overwriting; the conflict does not undo model calls or tool calls already made. Metadata/title updates do not change the revision.

Pydantic AI serializes history with ModelMessagesTypeAdapter (to_jsonable_python / validate_python, or to_json / validate_json); the format is Pydantic AI's own provider-neutral message model, with provider-specific details (e.g. signed reasoning) kept inside parts. JSON round-trips lose non-JSON-native types in tool returns (tuple to list, datetime to string). Compatibility promise: no migration needed when a message part is added; no version field documented; one known cross-version loader flag (rebuild_unrecorded_tool_files).
nodes.limitations: Message-history page read only first 100k of 154k characters, and as a tool summary.

nodes.text: Pydantic AI's caller supplies the conversation_id; scope= restricts reads to an owner (e.g. user id); saving a new conversation under an existing id raises a conflict.

LangGraph persists conversation history as graph state in checkpoints keyed by thread_id (short-term, thread-level memory); the Store (BaseStore: get, put, search, delete, batch over tuple namespaces) is for long-term cross-thread memory. H3 confirmed. Checkpointer backends: InMemorySaver, SqliteSaver, PostgresSaver, plus MongoDB, Redis, Oracle.

LangGraph BaseCheckpointSaver exposes get_tuple, put, put_writes, list, delete_thread (plus async variants); default serde is JsonPlusSerializer; the Checkpoint dict carries an integer format version field v. The unit stored is a graph-state snapshot, not a message log, so it is coupled to graph state schema.
nodes.limitations: Docstring says v is 1 but code sets LATEST_VERSION=2. Async variants and per-backend schema not read. Graph checkpointing is another scout's scope.

nodes.text: Across the three libraries the host owns the session/thread id and authorization; none enforces isolation itself except optional scope= in Pydantic AI. Only Pydantic AI documents optimistic conflict detection for concurrent turns; OpenAI only locks individual operations.

Design implication: for host embedding, the simplest protocol is item-level async (OpenAI shape: get/add/pop/clear), while Pydantic AI's revisioned record+entries log is the more robust concurrency design; a provider-neutral, version-tagged envelope for stored messages is something none of the three documents fully.
